string-array.name: quote_texts
string-array.item: You have power over your mind — not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
Freedom is not procured by a full enjoyment of what is desired, but by controlling the desire.
It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.
Most powerful is he who has himself in his own power.
No man is free who is not master of himself.
Resist the beginnings; the remedy comes too late.
The first and greatest victory is to conquer yourself.
I count him braver who overcomes his desires than him who conquers his enemies.
He who conquers others is strong; he who conquers himself is mighty.
Though he conquer a thousand men, he who conquers himself is the greatest victor.
Would you have a great empire? Rule over yourself.
It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a lot of it.
You could leave life right now. Let that determine what you do, say and think.
The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
While we are postponing, life speeds by.
First say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.
Concentrate every minute like a Roman on doing what\'s in front of you.
We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.
Do nothing which is of no use.
My experience is what I agree to attend to.
Attention is the beginning of devotion.
A wealth of information creates a poverty of attention.
How we spend our days is, of course, how we spend our lives.
All of humanity\'s problems stem from man\'s inability to sit quietly in a room alone.
The cost of a thing is the amount of life you exchange for it.
Everybody worships. The only choice we get is what to worship.
The modern devil is cheap dopamine.
If you love life, don\'t waste time, for time is what life is made up of.
Control of consciousness determines the quality of life.
Clarity about what matters provides clarity about what does not.
Tell me, what is it you plan to do with your one wild and precious life?
We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
You do not rise to the level of your goals. You fall to the level of your systems.
Every action you take is a vote for the person you wish to become.
The pain of discipline weighs ounces. The pain of regret weighs tons.
Hard choices, easy life. Easy choices, hard life.
Discipline is choosing between what you want now and what you want most.
Self-control is strength. Right thought is mastery. Calmness is power.
The version of you who set this block knew something. Listen to him.
This craving passes in about ninety seconds. Outlast it.
In an hour you won\'t remember wanting this. You will remember beating it.
You are not being deprived. You are being protected — by yourself.
The urge is loud because it is losing.
You have done harder things than closing a screen.
Relapse starts with one negotiation. This is it. Say no here.
The feed never ends. Your time does.
Nothing on that app will matter in a week. What you do instead might.
Real life is happening right now, off this screen.
Boredom is where your best ideas are hiding. Let yourself be bored.
That app is engineered to hook you. You saw it coming — that\'s why you\'re here.
Every scroll you skip is a rep for your willpower.
Progress, not perfection. Closing this screen counts.
Your attention is the most valuable thing you own. Spend it on purpose.
Don\'t trade this evening for a dopamine hit.
Losing once does not mean losing today. Close this and keep the day.

Your phone stopped the blocker, and more than one thing does that: clearing memory in the background, the moment right after AppBlocker updates itself, or — on Xiaomi — switching between spaces. The family filter sits underneath the app, in your phone\'s own DNS, so it carried on refusing bad sites for the whole time this was down. What stopped was app blocking, schedules and the danger hour — not everything.

Android still shows the switch as on, which is why it looked fine and blocked nothing. That switch remembers what you chose — it doesn\'t check whether the blocker is actually running. Now the app checks, and tells you.

The alert that brought you here pops up over whatever you\'re doing and comes back every few minutes until blocking is running again. But your phone keeps “Floating notifications” as its own switch, and it\'s off by default for most apps — while it\'s off, the alert can only sit silently in the shade. This is the one thing AppBlocker can\'t switch on for you.
Why the app can\'t do this for you

Android doesn\'t let an app switch its own blocking back on. That rule is what stops a bad app from quietly switching itself on and watching your screen — and it\'s the same rule that stops this one from switching itself back. It has to be your tap.
A much faster way to do it

In Settings ▸ Accessibility ▸ AppBlocker there\'s a Shortcut option. Turn it on and pick the volume keys. After that, holding both volume keys for three seconds switches the blocker off, and holding them again switches it back on — from anywhere, without hunting through Settings.
The blocker is running and watching again. Nothing else to do.
It\'s switched on in Settings, but it isn\'t running — so nothing is being blocked right now.

Your phone\'s family DNS filter is not running, so nothing is being filtered at the network level. Browsers stay closed until it is back on — everything else on your phone still works. Open AppBlocker to switch it back on.
Your phone is sending every lookup to the family filter. Adult sites are blocked before they load, in every app — not just the ones the blocker can read.
Nothing is being filtered at the network level. The blocker still watches your screen, but anything it cannot read gets through.
Private DNS is on, but it isn\'t filtering
Your phone is using an encrypted lookup, which is good — but the server it uses doesn\'t block anything. Encrypted is not the same as filtered. Paste the address below instead.
This phone is too old for it
This needs Android 9 or newer. Everything else in the app works as normal.

Before your phone can open any site, it has to ask where that site is. This filter answers that question — and refuses to answer it for adult sites. It works underneath everything: every app, every browser, pictures inside an app, and pages the blocker can\'t read a word of.
It also can\'t be killed by your phone\'s battery manager, because it isn\'t an app — it\'s a setting. That is the one thing the rest of the blocker cannot promise you.
Find Private DNS. It is usually under Network and internet; on Xiaomi it is under Connection and sharing.
Choose Private DNS provider hostname and paste the address.
Save, then come back here. This page turns green when the app can see it working.

This filter blocks whole categories, not just adult sites — including dynamic-DNS addresses, which are often used to get around filters. That is usually what you want. If an app ever stops reaching its own server while the filter is on, this is why: check Profile ▸ What the blocker sees, which now says so plainly.
Copied — now paste it into Private DNS
Why the app can\'t switch it on for you

Android doesn\'t let an app change this setting — the same rule that stops a bad app from quietly redirecting everything you look up. It has to be your tap. The app can see it, and defend it, but it cannot set it.

You asked for a filter you couldn\'t switch off. No app on Android can be that — so switching it off costs you the browsers instead. Every browser closes until the filter is back on. Maps, your bank, messages and everything else keep working, and the app waits a minute before acting so a normal network change never costs you anything.
That only starts once the app has seen the filter working at least once. Until then it just asks.
